$schema_note: ECS Fargate task definition for the DAILY CORE-FACILITY USAGE INFERENCE run over core 14 (Research Informatics) — `python -m pipeline_cores.run --core 14 --with-affinity --alias-search --llm-carry-forward --with-llm --llm-triage-candidates-only --with-method-families --reconcile`. Scheduled by EventBridge rule `reciterai-cores-daily` (05:00 UTC, see eventbridge.json) as a direct RunTask target — EventBridge Input is NOT forwarded to ECS targets, so the default command below IS the invocation (deploy_cron.sh ecs branch). Uses the SAME Dockerfile + ECR repo as the enrichment/cold/grants/spotlight tasks (the repo's single Dockerfile `COPY . .` already contains pipeline_cores); this task def only overrides the default CMD. LOG GROUP `/ecs/reciterai-cores` MUST be pre-created — `ecsTaskExecutionRole` lacks `logs:CreateLogGroup`, so `awslogs-create-group` is intentionally omitted (ECS rejects `false`; only `true`-or-omit — the same caveat as cold/spotlight/grants). SECRETS: the four DB_* keys (utils.db.get_engine reads DB_HOST/DB_USERNAME/DB_PASSWORD/DB_NAME from the env and connects to ReciterDB over MySQL) plus AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK. NO OPENAI_API_KEY, unlike enrichment/cold: nothing in pipeline_cores has an OpenAI path (no import, no content-filter fallback), and injecting an unread credential is surface for nothing. NO S3 either — this pipeline publishes no artifact; its output is the DynamoDB (publication, core) rows SPS's nightly projects into MySQL, so there is no `latest/` pointer and no shrink guard here. `--reconcile` (2026-09-29) closes the one gap a re-score cannot: run.py persists only confirmed/candidate rows, so a pair the nightly stops surfacing kept its old status forever. After `put_core_usage`, the sweep demotes to `below_threshold` every core-14 candidate/confirmed row whose `scored_at` is older than this run's single stamp — out-of-corpus pairs included — through a conditional UpdateItem (`status IN (candidate, confirmed) AND scored_at = :seen`), so a human `claimed`/`rejected` and a concurrently re-scored row are never overwritten. It refuses a core this run surfaced ZERO rows for and a core whose would-demote count exceeds half of (demoted + re-surfaced), logging `reconcile: core 14 REFUSED` at ERROR; otherwise it logs `reconcile: core 14 demoted X, skipped Y (condition failed)`. run.py refuses the flag outright on `--test`/`--pmids-file`, so the plumbing-gate overrides below must DROP `--reconcile` when they add `--test 500`. LLM (#412, 2026-10-01): `--with-llm` is ON, but only with `--llm-triage-candidates-only`, which spends Bedrock solely on unscored pubs a no-LLM pass already surfaces (new candidates, a handful a night), never on the ~80k corpus; LLM rejections are persisted below_threshold so they are never re-triaged, and the LLM can never be the deciding vote for confirmation (#414). deploy_notes.llm_evidence_and_bedrock below predates this and describes the zero-Bedrock nightly. WHAT THE COMMAND DELIBERATELY OMITS is as load-bearing as what it contains: `--all-cores-screen` is ABSENT (EXPERIMENTAL per its own --help: one Haiku call screens every core at once for ~13x fewer screen calls, but it lost 7-11% screen recall on the 237-pilot and its borderline true positives collapse to score 1 — off until re-calibrated to per-core parity), and `pipeline_cores.batch_screen` is NOT in the command at all: batch_screen MINTS candidate rows through persist.put_candidate and overwrites `likelihood`, which is a different (and screen-priced) product from run.py's evidence-weight scoring — the nightly runs run.py and only run.py.

placeholders.{TASK_ROLE_ARN}: arn:aws:iam::{ACCOUNT_ID}:role/reciterai-cores-task — IAM role attached to the running container; carries the policy in `cores_task_iam_policy.json` (DynamoDB CRUD on `reciterai` + CloudWatch Logs on `/ecs/reciterai-cores`, and nothing else). A NEW role: every existing task role is a superset in the wrong direction — enrichment/cold carry Secrets Manager grants this task does not need, and cold/grants carry S3 write grants to buckets this pipeline never publishes to. Three DynamoDB call shapes are exercised and they are the whole surface: `UpdateItem` (persist.put_core_usage, one per surfaced row), `Scan` (persist.scan_prior_core_usage for the affinity prior, and the carry-forward read of stored LLM evidence), and `GetItem` (persist.get_curated_clients on PK=CORE#14 / SK=CLIENTS). `--reconcile` adds no new call shape: one more paginated `Scan` (persist.scan_stale_core_rows) and one conditional `UpdateItem` per stale row (persist.demote_stale_core_rows), both already granted.
placeholders.{EXECUTION_ROLE_ARN}: arn:aws:iam::{ACCOUNT_ID}:role/ecsTaskExecutionRole — the standard ECS task execution role, reused unchanged from the enrichment deploy. Needs ECR pull + CloudWatch Logs (AWS-managed `AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy`) and its existing inline `secretsmanager:GetSecretValue` grant on `reciterai/reciter-analysis-db` + `reciterai/bedrock-api-key` — both already present since the enrichment/cold deploys, so NO extension is needed for this family (the first new family in a while that needs none). The execution role — not the task role — injects the `secrets[]` env vars at container start, which is why `cores_task_iam_policy.json` has no SecretsManager statement at all.
placeholders.{IMAGE_URI}: ECR image URI in the `reciterai-enrichment` repo, e.g. `{ACCOUNT_ID}.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/reciterai-enrichment:{TAG}`, built `docker build --platform linux/amd64` (the task is X86_64; a Mac defaults to arm64, which won't run on Fargate). The Dockerfile `COPY . .` already includes `pipeline_cores` — no new build pipeline. Config is image-baked (#204), and for THIS pipeline that is a bigger surface than usual: `config/core_dictionary.yaml` (core 14's three aliases, their cached `alias_hits` PMC counts, the staff CWIDs signal 2 joins on, the per-core thresholds) and `combine.WEIGHTS` (the fitted evidence weights) all ride the image, so any dictionary or weight change needs a rebuild + push before the next tick sees it. The ONE piece of per-core configuration that does NOT need a rebuild is the curated known-client list: SPS's 'Known clients' panel writes it to DynamoDB (CORE#14/CLIENTS) and `run_core` unions it with the YAML list at run time, so a client added in SPS today is in scope tomorrow morning with no deploy.
placeholders.{DB_SECRET_ARN}: Full ARN of `reciterai/reciter-analysis-db` (JSON SecretString with DB_HOST/DB_USERNAME/DB_PASSWORD/DB_NAME keys). ECS pulls individual JSON keys via the trailing `:KEY::` syntax. Same secret as the enrichment and cold tasks — the cores corpus is the SAME ReciterDB analysis corpus the topic scorer reads (`utils.sql_queries.PUBLICATION_EXTRACTION_SQL`, joined by `ingest.fetch_publications`/`fetch_author_totals`), read-only.
placeholders.{NCBI_API_KEY_SECRET_ARN}: Full ARN of `reciterai/ncbi-api-key` (plain SecretString, an NCBI E-utilities API key). pmc_search reads NCBI_API_KEY and paces at 10 req/s instead of the anonymous 3 req/s that unkeyed Fargate egress shares per IP — the cause of the alias-search 429s in #415. Execution-role-injected like the Bedrock key; ecsTaskExecutionRole's reciterai-enrichment-secrets grant must list it.
placeholders.{BEDROCK_API_KEY_SECRET_ARN}: Full ARN of `reciterai/bedrock-api-key` (plain SecretString — a LONG-TERM Bedrock API key). boto3 auto-detects `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` and uses it as the bearer token for `bedrock-runtime` calls. Same secret as every other task. Referenced by the EXECUTION role (env injection), not the task role. It is injected on a command that makes ZERO Bedrock calls on purpose — see deploy_notes.llm_evidence_and_bedrock for why that costs nothing and what it buys.

deploy_notes.scope: ONE core. `--core 14` (Research Informatics) is the entire scope of the nightly: it is the core whose claim queue is staffed and reviewed, and the only core run.py has ever scored in production. Every other core stays operator-run from `python -m pipeline_cores.run` (all-cores if `--core` is omitted) exactly as today — this task does not change their cadence, and it cannot touch their rows, because a run only writes the (publication, core) pairs for the cores it scored. ponytail: the core id is hard-coded in the command string rather than driven by config. Ceiling is one core per task definition; the upgrade path when a second core is staffed is one line — either widen this command (`--core 14 --core 22` is NOT supported: run.py's --core takes a single id, so widening means dropping --core to run every core in the dictionary) or register a sibling family with its own rule, which is also how a second core gets its own schedule and its own log group. Do not reach for a loop in the command until there are three.
deploy_notes.sizing: 1 vCPU / 4 GB, sized on the CORPUS LOAD rather than on concurrency. With no `--pmids-file` the pool is None, so `ingest.fetch_publications` returns the whole scoreable corpus — 80,203 publications (the count is stated in `ingest.fetch_author_totals`' docstring), each with its title and abstract, held as one list for the life of the run; `ingest.fetch_author_bylines` then holds the byline map for those same PMIDs, and `run_core` builds a SignalResult plus a CoreUsageRecord per publication on top of both (twice for the not-yet-confirmed ones, since phase 2 re-combines them). Two full-table DynamoDB Scans layer on: `scan_prior_core_usage` for the affinity prior (`--with-affinity`) and the carry-forward read for the stored LLM evidence (`--llm-carry-forward`); both paginate with a server-side filter and a projection, so they cost pages and time, not another copy of the table. The first Fargate runs (2026-09-05) completed a full-corpus pass in ~42s at this size without an OOM, but MemoryUtilization was not captured, so the ceiling is still un-measured; the arithmetic puts peak in the 1-1.5 GB class next to the cold-run's measured ~300-500 MB on a 13x smaller (~6,200 PMID) corpus, so 4 GB is ~3x headroom, not a round number; the first tick's `MemoryUtilization` is the number that should replace this estimate. It is deliberately NOT 2 GB: run.py writes NOTHING until every core has finished (`put_core_usage` runs after the loop), so an OOM kill costs the entire night's scoring rather than half of it, and EventBridge does not retry a task that started and died — the failure is total, and silent until someone reads the log group. The 1 vCPU is for the corpus load, SQLAlchemy row marshalling, and JSON/TLS against DynamoDB + NCBI; the nightly command has no Bedrock fan-out at all, so this is NOT the cold-run's concurrency argument. The other reason not to drop to enrichment's 0.25 vCPU is the operator override below: `--with-llm` fans `signals.llm_triage` out over 8 threads (`--llm-workers` default), and 0.25 vCPU would head-of-line-stall JSON parse + TLS across that fan-out. Default 20 GB ephemeral storage is ample — `--alias-search` caches only the PMC XML for the PMIDs its three alias searches name (~27 documents for core 14's aliases) under `out/fulltext_cache/`, cold on every task because `--fulltext-s3` is not in the command. NOTE: there is no Fargate task timeout — a hung run runs forever (a stalled NCBI socket is the likeliest cause; utils.db already bounds a wedged ReciterDB connection per #224).
deploy_notes.llm_evidence_and_bedrock: WHY `--with-llm` IS ABSENT, and why `--llm-carry-forward` is not optional in its place. (1) Cost: `signals.llm_triage` makes one Haiku screen call per publication it is handed and a Sonnet dense-score call for each one at or above SCREEN_CUTOFF. Over an unscoped run that is one screen per CORPUS publication — ~80,203 Haiku calls a night, plus the Sonnet tail. How much Bedrock a nightly may spend is an open decision tracked in its own GitHub issue, so the shipped schedule spends ZERO. (2) Safety: `persist.put_core_usage` SETs what the run produced and REMOVEs every `_OWNED_ATTRS` attribute it did NOT (`ack_alias`, `ack_snippet`, `llm_score`, `llm_rationale`, `author_affinity`) — deliberate, from #384, so a previous run's `llm_rationale` cannot survive on a pair scored without the LLM and read as fresh evidence. The consequence is that a nightly without `--with-llm` would STRIP `llm_score`/`llm_rationale` from every row it re-surfaces, and on core 14 that is the chip the review queue rests on (62 of 62 open rows carry it). `--llm-carry-forward` reads the stored values back and re-emits them, so the REMOVE has nothing to strip: it is what makes a zero-Bedrock nightly non-destructive, and dropping it from this command silently empties the queue's LLM evidence on the first tick. (3) The Bedrock secret is injected anyway, and it costs nothing: the value is fetched by the EXECUTION role at container start (the task role has no SecretsManager statement), and that role already holds the `GetSecretValue` grant on `reciterai/bedrock-api-key` from the enrichment deploy — nothing new is granted here, and an unused env var is not a call. What it buys is the override path: an operator can run a one-off LLM re-score with `aws ecs run-task --overrides` against the REGISTERED definition (typically `--pmids-file`-scoped to an existing candidate pool — running the LLM over 80k publications to rank a few hundred is the trade `read_pmids_file`'s docstring exists to warn about), with no new task-definition revision, no secret plumbing, and no IAM change. Making LLM-on the STANDING nightly is a command edit + `register-task-definition` — still no new infra, and still no IAM change, because Bedrock authenticates on the bearer token and the task role deliberately carries no `bedrock:InvokeModel`.
deploy_notes.plumbing_gate: Two bounded runs, in this order. The first is free and writes nothing; the second is the only one that proves the write. (Both gate commands deliberately OMIT `--reconcile`: run.py refuses it with `--test`, because a 500-publication slice would read every other open row as stale.) (1) `aws ecs run-task ... --overrides '{"containerOverrides":[{"name":"reciterai-cores","command":["sh","-c","python -m pipeline_cores.run --core 14 --test 500 --with-affinity --alias-search --llm-carry-forward --dry-run"]}]}'`. `--test 500` is appended as a LIMIT after the corpus query's `ORDER BY a1.pmid DESC`, so it is the 500 most recent publications — a recency slice, not a random sample — which is enough to prove the image carries pipeline_cores + `config/core_dictionary.yaml`, that ReciterDB is reachable from the chosen subnets with the injected DB_* secrets, that NCBI egress works (the alias search prints `[14 Research Informatics] alias search: N PMC papers name an alias`), that the task role can `dynamodb:Scan` — BOTH Scans run under `--dry-run`, deliberately: the affinity prior's (`run_core`'s docstring says so) and the carry-forward's (`main()`'s comment says why — skipping it would make a dry run report triaging the whole corpus where the real run triages a few hundred, under-reporting Bedrock spend by two orders of magnitude). The carry-forward Scan also RAISES rather than degrading to `{}`, so this gate proves that read hard: a missing `dynamodb:Scan` fails the container instead of quietly returning nothing, and that CloudWatch logging lands in `/ecs/reciterai-cores`. It ends at `DRY RUN — N records would be written` having written nothing. What it CANNOT prove: `dynamodb:UpdateItem`, and the curated-client `GetItem`, which `run_core` deliberately skips under `--dry-run` (it prints `[14 Research Informatics] dry-run: skipping DynamoDB curated-client read`) — i.e. the two permissions most likely to be missing from a brand-new task role are exactly the two this gate is blind to. (2) The SAME command without `--dry-run`. Understand what it does before running it against production: it is a REAL SCORING RUN over the 500-publication slice, and inside that slice it both demotes and deletes. `put_core_usage` rewrites `status`, so a stored `confirmed` re-scores to `candidate` (the branch's own test `test_put_core_usage_can_still_move_an_engine_status` pins exactly that), and every write carries a REMOVE clause over the `_OWNED_ATTRS` attributes this run did not produce — the #384 sweep described in `llm_evidence_and_bedrock` above. What IS bounded is the blast radius, not the damage: run.py persists only `confirmed`/`candidate` records and `put_core_usage` is a per-row UpdateItem, so every pair OUTSIDE the 500-publication slice is untouched, and the two human statuses are protected by the ConditionExpression inside it. Run gate (1) first and read its `llm: <n> carried forward` line: if `<n>` is 0 there, do not run gate (2) — carry-forward found nothing and this gate would strip the LLM chips off whatever it surfaces. That is what proves UpdateItem + GetItem end to end, and it is cheap because the surfaced count out of 500 recent publications is a handful. NEITHER gate measures wall clock at corpus scale — `--test` caps the corpus, so the full 80,203-publication pass the 05:00 schedule assumes is first measured by the first real tick (infra/README.md, 'Cores daily run launch path', step 6).
